summary: Planned the criteria 9-13 reconciliation: one shared Core contract module both host-blocked paths resolve to (blocked-resumable + one honest message), rejecting the done-terminal and distinguish-the-block-reason alternatives; 6 ordered steps with per-step verification and a permanent coherence regression test.

details.approach: Approach A — a new pure Core module (src/core/orchestrator/pipeline/host-blocked-merge.ts) owns the single host-blocked hand-off contract (BlockCategories.awaiting_human + one honest message). auto-merge gains a `needs_human_merge` case in autoMergeNext routing to {go:'block', category, needed} and drops notifyHostBlockedMerge; the poller takes its needed/notification text from the same module. No schema change, no new BlockCategory, no new PrEvent, no new API call.
rejected: Approach B (distinguish required-review vs no-merge-permission and branch the message) — needs GraphQL reviewDecision or an extra branch-protection call plus identity matching; buys a nicer message and no lifecycle correctness. The owner offered wording-that-holds as an equal alternative.
Approach C (make the poller terminal to match auto-merge) — `done` is the worse contract on every axis the owner named.
two_findings_prior_phases_missed: go:'done' is not a neutral hand-off: handleCompletedOutcome (task-scheduler.ts:233-277) destroys the worktree via cleanupWorkspace, makes the task non-retryable (completed is not in RETRYABLE_STATES), and posts the ticket comment 'Task completed successfully.' on an unmerged PR. Criterion 10's 'false completed' is a literal message the engine emits.

blockTask (orchestrator/index.ts:449-458) ALREADY delivers the block's `needed` to chat + ticket via deliverBlockedQuestion for awaiting_human. So routing auto-merge to `block` while keeping notifyHostBlockedMerge would post two ticket comments for one event — the naive implementation of the chosen contract has this bug baked in. The plan deletes the notify.
premortem: F1 double owner message (mitigated: delete notifyHostBlockedMerge; the block's needed is the single message)
F2 approval-dismissed nuance lost (mitigated: thread pr_number + approval_dismissed through result.data so the pure `next` can pick the variant)

F3 a PR merely awaiting its required review also reports mergeable_state=blocked — escalating on `blocked` alone would break the normal review wait (mitigated: the existing /approve + green gates are preserved verbatim, plus a new regression test that a blocked PR with no /approve does nothing)
F4 the optional allowlist could stall a genuine merge (mitigated: step 5 is last, isolated, droppable, with a per-state matrix)

F5 accepted: awaiting_human is self-unblock eligible, so a permanently-blocked task may re-check every ~8h and never reach the 48h `failed` escalation. No rework, no branch push, no fast loop — and a lap merges the PR by itself once the owner approves. Rejected a new BlockCategory (schema growth + shared health-monitor change + it would misrepresent a merge block as a discretionary decision). This is already today's poller behavior.
details.scope_declined: Research §24's third path (formally-approved + green + host-blocked PR with no /approve comment emits no event, so it waits with a misleading 'waiting for review' reminder). Outside the owner's stated ask, does not loop or rework, and closing it risks the highest-traffic path (F3). Recommended as its own ticket.

verification.gates: pnpm test:all && pnpm run lint && pnpm run typecheck
verification.per_step: targeted vitest runs on auto-merge.test.ts, pr-event-poller.test.ts, the new host-blocked-merge-contract.test.ts, and github-hosting.test.ts
verification.node_modules: installed in this worktree — the prior phases' 'run pnpm install first' note is stale

details.open_questions: none — every remaining fork (which contract, distinguish-vs-word, the optional allowlist) was explicitly delegated to design by the owner
